title: Batch metadata writers store an object the registry refuses and report it saved (registry-dependent refusals only logged)
body:
domain:server#2 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufziCTpjnYbdh76SAWwb

Origin: out-of-scope measurement of the #32312 card thread (PR #32368). Filed by the seat that ruled the single-save half there.

Premise re-check: `git grep -n "console.warn" -- packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-hydration.ts` shows the registration-refusal warn in `applyObjectRegistryMutation`, and `git grep -n "bodyOnly" -- packages/metadata-protocol/src` shows the batch faces still pre-flighting body-only.

Clause-②: the claiming seat declares it (a batch that reported success now reports a failed row: narrowing).


## What happens

A batch writer of `object` rows calls `saveMetaItem` in publish mode with the body-only registry pre-flight (#29673). A refusal that reads the registry's other objects (ADR-0144 D6's roll-up door, and the D2/D6 follow door from #32312) is not asked there. The row is stored, the call resolves `success: true`, and the registration refusal at `applyObjectRegistryMutation` (`protocol-registry-hydration.ts`) is only `console.warn`ed. The object is left unregistered (new) or as it was (re-save). This is the #6995 silent-divergence class: the stored row and the registry disagree, and the caller is told the write succeeded.

## Measured (#32312 branch, sealed dogfood stack, 2026-11-10)

`protocol.saveMetaItem({ type: 'object', mode: 'publish', writeFace, item })` with a child amount following `invoice.title` (a `text` field with no code), parent `rcf_invoice` registered:

| writeFace | call | row stored | registered | heard |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `package-duplicate` | resolved `success: true` | yes | no | `console.warn` only |
| `package-unmanaged-import` | resolved `success: true` | yes | no | `console.warn` only |
| `external-import` | resolved `success: true` | yes | no | `console.warn` only |
| none (internal callers: migration passes, CLI ownership, install-local) | resolved `success: true` | yes | no | `console.warn` only |

The `/meta` single-save faces (`meta-envelope`, `meta-dispatch`) answer 422 and store nothing since #32312 (ruling B).

## Why it is not a one-line fix

#29673's reason holds for a batch: a sibling later in the same batch can complete or break the pair, so asking the registry before each row is wrong both ways. The fix belongs at the batch's end: after the batch's registrations, relay each registration refusal into the batch's result (`failed[]` for duplicate/import, the install report for install-local) and decide whether the stored row is rolled back or flagged. That decision (roll back vs. keep-and-flag) is a design call.

## Acceptance

- Each batch face named above reports a registration refusal of a row it wrote, per row, in its own result shape; none reports such a row as copied/imported/installed.
- Whatever the rollback ruling, the stored rows and the registry agree after the batch, or the disagreement is reported.
- A batch whose sibling completes the pair later in the same batch still succeeds (the #29673 case, pinned).
